summary.text: A 24-year-old female was hospitalized with recurrent headache and chest and back pain. Since age 7 she had recurrent headaches with fever, a local diagnosis of meningitis that improved with infusion treatment, chest and back burning pain from age 12, and gradually decreasing left hearing from age 13. Later worsening with coma led to antituberculosis treatment for over a year; she stopped the drugs about 7 months before admission, and symptoms recurred three days before admission after a cold.

Neurological examination showed neck strength of 2 fingers with negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs, and left hearing loss was found. Brain CT showed right basal ganglia encephalomalacia and supratentorial hydrocephalus, C-reactive protein was 57.30 mg/L, and a lumbar puncture on September 16 with serial CSF results led to a diagnosis of suppurative meningitis. MRI of the brain and spinal cord was obtained, and PMseq-DNA showed group G + Streptococcus.

Ceftriaxone sodium was given and vancomycin and betamethasone were added, after which CSF leukocytes and protein decreased and headache remitted. Otorhinolaryngology consultation found no auricle deformity, audiometry suggested neurological deafness, and HRCT of the temporal bone showed increased left mastoid air chamber density and a narrower left internal auditory canal. Congenital inner ear malformation was considered and surgery recommended.

After a preoperative examination on November 27, left stapes resection under an otoendoscope, fenestration of the inner ear, repair of CSF otorrhea and temporal muscle removal were performed; CSF leakage at the stapes footplate was found and the CSF no longer exuded afterwards. Incomplete partition Type I inner ear malformation was diagnosed, and she was followed up for 1 year without recurrent headaches or chest or back pain.
